commands.review_summary:
Adds menu and Settings entry points for previewing, copying, and saving a locally generated 1200×630 multi-provider subscription usage card plus plain-text stats.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: configure more than one visible Codex account with distinct snapshots, then open Share Stats; the branch maps Codex to one provider-level source rather than all visible account snapshots. This was not live-run in the read-only Linux review environment.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A maintainer must first approve or decline the permanent sharing surface; if approved, the contributor should repair account aggregation and provide inspectable native-app proof.

target.title: Add shareable subscription usage cards
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar already computes local token and estimated-cost history, but the current menu is a poor sharing surface: the numbers cannot be copied as one artifact, and a menu screenshot is fragile and difficult to read. This PR turns the existing local data into a fixed 1200×630 card plus a plain-text equivalent.

The intentionally narrow v1 is **local export**, not a hosted profile:

- no account system, public URL, upload, tracking, or backend;
- no prompt, project, path, email, or account identity in the payload;
- no attempt to make unlike measurements look complete—unknown spend remains unknown;
- one immutable payload drives preview, PNG, clipboard text, and saved image.

Alternatives considered:

- **Screenshot the current menu:** low implementation cost, but clips, changes size, and mixes controls with the artifact.
- **Hosted share link / OG page:** easier to repost, but introduces persistence, deletion, abuse, and privacy policy work that is not justified for v1.
- **Provider-by-provider exports:** simpler aggregation, but fails the core use case of comparing all enabled AI subscriptions in one picture.

## What this adds

- A native **Share Stats…** action in the status menu and Settings → Menu → Sharing.
- A 1200×630 local card with combined 30-day tracked tokens and estimated spend.
- Visually separate **By subscription** and **Top models** rankings.
- Model rankings built from real daily `modelBreakdowns`, with provider attribution.
- **Copy Image**, **Copy Stats**, and **Save…** actions from one preview.
- Existing CodexBar colors, typography, localization patterns, menu descriptors, and lifecycle handling.

## Data contract

| Surface | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tracked tokens | Sum of known local token-history snapshots in the selected 30-day window. |
| Estimated spend | Sum of finite priced history only; the card reports priced-source coverage. |
| Subscription row | One enabled provider source in the current draft. Missing local history reads `connected`, never `$0`. |
| Top models | Cross-provider aggregation of real model breakdowns for the same window. |
| Daily bars | Aggregate tracked tokens by local calendar day. |

### Open account-scope blocker

ClawSweeper correctly identified that CodexBar can retain multiple visible Codex account snapshots while this draft currently exports one provider-level snapshot. The intended product contract is account-complete sharing—every visible account must contribute without exposing account identity—but that repair and focused multi-account regression coverage are still required before this draft is merge-ready. The narrower active-account behavior is not being presented as complete.

## Privacy allowlist

The export payload permits provider display name, aggregate tokens, aggregate estimated cost, active-day counts, model name, period end, and daily aggregate token counts. It does not carry email, account ID, project name/path, prompt text, session title, file content, credentials, or raw event records. Rendering and pasteboard/save operations are local.

## Relationship to the Settings dashboard

- Companion draft: [#2116 — Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2116)
- This PR owns the share/export workflow only.
- #2116 owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime; they are split so maintainers can approve, revise, or decline either product surface independently.

## Verification

- [x] `swift build`
- [x] `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` — 3 tests pass
- [x] `make check`
- [x] Exact 1200×630 PNG render visually inspected with four enabled providers and real model breakdowns
- [x] PNG pasteboard type verified on macOS
- [ ] Account-complete multi-account regression coverage
- [ ] Sanitized bundled-app proof for both entry points and Copy Image / Copy Stats / Save
- [ ] Full sharded suite in CI

`Scripts/package_app.sh` completed the main Release build. The optional widget step is blocked on this machine by a local Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plugin-version mismatch; a no-widget bundle was packaged and launched successfully.

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. This draft asks maintainers to decide whether privacy-first local sharing belongs in CodexBar and confirms the proposed account-complete scope. It should remain a draft until that decision, the multi-account repair, and inspectable sanitized proof are complete.
